note: Striatal PDE10A inhibition reproduces D2-antagonist pharmacology in rodent antipsychotic screens; four sponsors took selective inhibitors into schizophrenia trials and none showed antipsychotic efficacy.
label: Schizophrenia (PDE10A)

engagement.model: Rodent striatal cAMP/cGMP signalling and PET occupancy
engagement.note: Rodent striatum: PDE10A inhibitors raised cyclic-nucleotide signalling in both D1 and D2 pathways; no patient read-out yet.
engagement.quote: Biochemical characterization of these compounds has shown that PDE10A inhibitors modulate both the dopamine D1-direct and D2-indirect striatal pathways and regulate the phosphorylation status of a panel of glutamate receptor subunits in the striatum.

engagement.model: Rodent striatal cAMP/cGMP signalling and PET occupancy
engagement.note: Human [11C]T-773 PET: putamen occupancy 2.8–72% across 3–1000 mg, dose- and concentration-dependent, as the monkey PET with the same ligand predicted.
engagement.quote: PDE10A occupancy in the putamen ranged from 2.8% to 72.1% at 3hours after a single administration of 3 to 1000mg of TAK-063, and increased in a dose- and plasma concentration-dependent manner.
engagement.reason: Human PET occupancy matched primate model
engagement.judgement: Call: the rhesus PET with the same [11C]T-773 ligand (Takano 2016 Synapse, 10.1002/syn.21896) predicted measurable dose-dependent striatal occupancy and the human study delivered it. The abstract does not state a cross-species comparison, the full text is paywalled, and subjects were healthy volunteers, not patients. Pfizer's [18F]MNI-659 PET (Delnomdedieu 2017, 10.1016/j.neuropharm.2017.01.016) independently showed 45–63% striatal occupancy at 20 mg. A stricter reader could leave this untested.

dose.note: Takeda set the efficacious exposure from rat MK-801 hyperlocomotion at 0.3–1 mg/kg; Pfizer had done the same from rat CAR.
dose.quote: TAK-063 at 0.3 and 1 mg/kg p.o., strongly suppressed MK-801 [(5R,10S)-(+)-5-methyl-10,11-dihydro-5H-dibenzo[a,d]cyclohepten-5,10-imine]-induced hyperlocomotion, which is often used as a predictive model for antipsychotic-like activity in rodents.

dose.note: Patient exposures sat inside the rodent-predicted efficacious range (human PET: 45–63% occupancy at 20 mg) yet no efficacy; MK-8189 later failed at ~80% occupancy.
dose.quote: Treatment was well tolerated, and observed PF-02545920 exposures were within the range predicted to be adequate for demonstrating efficacy. However, no significant differences in the prespecified efficacy end points between the 2 PF-02545920 treatment arms and placebo were observed.
dose.judgement: Call: the question is whether the rodent-derived exposure target held. It was reached (PK adequate; Delnomdedieu 2017 PET put 20 mg at 45–63% occupancy) and produced nothing, so the target itself was wrong; a reader who scores 'exposure achieved as predicted' would mark this same. Walling 2019 (monotherapy) says the same: 'Pharmacokinetics exposures seemed adequate for binding/inhibiting PDE10A enzyme.' Year is the 2019 paper; the trials ran 2010–2013. Mukai 2026 (10.1097/JCP.0000000000002152) repeated it: 24 mg MK-8189 predicted ~80% sustained occupancy against an animal-model threshold of >50%, and failed. The model's first use for dose is dated 2015 because Schmidt 2008's abstract carries no quotable exposure sentence, although Pfizer set its clinical doses from the same rodent models.

efficacy.note: Pfizer's TP-10/MP-10 blocked conditioned avoidance and psychostimulant hyperactivity in rats, the D2-antagonist screens; no patient data.
efficacy.quote: These new pharmacological tools enabled studies that provide further evidence that inhibition of PDE10A represents an important new target for the treatment of schizophrenia and related disorders of basal ganglia function.

efficacy.note: PF-02545920 5/15 mg Q12H no better than placebo while risperidone was; TAK-063 (2019), RG7203 (2021) and MK-8189 (2026) failed too.
efficacy.quote: This indicates that PDE10A inhibition does not produce an antipsychotic effect in patients with acute exacerbation of schizophrenia.
efficacy.reason: Rodent screens positive; four drugs failed
efficacy.judgement: Walling 2019 chosen over Macek 2019 (online Sept 2018, 10.1016/j.schres.2018.08.028) because it had an active comparator that separated and states the conclusion outright; Macek missed its primary endpoint but hedges ('may be suggestive of antipsychotic activity'). Registry results for the Pfizer trial (NCT01175135) were posted 2018-03-20, so the contra could be dated 2018 under a registry-first rule. Umbricht 2021 (10.1016/j.bpsgos.2021.03.001): RG7203 worsened reward learning in negative-symptom patients. Mukai 2024 (10.1016/j.schres.2024.05.019) saw a trend at 12 mg; Mukai 2026 phase 2b failed at 16/24 mg. Lu AF11167 omitted: no published comparison found.

safety.note: Rat catalepsy, prolactin and glucose screens predicted a tolerability edge over D2 antagonists; only weak catalepsy at 3 mg/kg.
safety.quote: At 3 mg/kg p.o., TAK-063 elicited a weak cataleptic response compared with haloperidol and olanzapine.

safety.note: Akathisia and dystonia exceeded placebo on 20 mg TAK-063; dystonia 6/74 on 15 mg PF-02545920 vs 3/74 placebo; EPS again with MK-8189.
safety.short: EPS in patients at non-efficacious doses
safety.quote: No deaths occurred, and the incidence of akathisia and dystonia, categories of extrapyramidal syndromes, was more frequent in the TAK-063 group than placebo.
safety.reason: Rat predicted tolerability edge; EPS appeared
safety.judgement: Call: the rat screen flagged only weak catalepsy at ~10× the efficacious dose and the pivotal paper concluded 'potential for superior safety and tolerability profiles'; patients showed akathisia/dystonia above placebo at a dose that did not produce efficacy, inverting the predicted therapeutic index. Walling 2019 reports dystonia in 1, 6, 0 and 3 patients (5 mg, 15 mg, risperidone, placebo), matching the NCT01175135 registry (0.01/0.08/0.00/0.04). A reader who counts the weak rat signal as a prediction could score this same. Macek 2019 full text paywalled; abstract-level reading.
